ai.description: This snake reaches 20–25 cm in length. It is uniform dark brown to black dorsally with a pale yellow belly and a blunt, shield-like tail ending in a small, hardened terminal scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhinophis fergusonianus* is best distinguished by its unique, sharply truncated tail ending in a large, flat, circular shield that is distinctly broader than the body.
ai.habitat: *Rhinophis fergusonianus* inhabits the moist, high-altitude evergreen forests of the Cardamom Hills in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Cardamom Hills earth snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through moist soil to forage for earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhinophis fergusonianus* is ovoviviparous, producing small litters of 3–4 live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Rhinophis fergusonianus is endemic to the Cardamom Hills of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500m.
